modelIntro.title: What Is Wan 2.5 AI Video Generator?
description: Wan 2.5 is the lower-cost Wan option on Toolaze. It helps you test whether an ad hook, product angle, poster treatment, thumbnail variant, or still-image animation deserves another render.
Use it for quick idea checks: create small trials, keep two or three promising directions, reject crowded attempts, and save notes for the concept worth developing further.

howToUse.title: How to Test Wan 2.5 Ideas at Lower Cost

steps.title: Choose one clear test
steps.desc: Use one run to answer a practical question: does the product turn read, does the opening hook stand out, does the poster motion feel useful, or does the sound cue match the material?

steps.title: Write a small motion brief
steps.desc: Name one subject, one camera move, and one texture or sound cue. Keep the action simple so the result is easy to judge.

steps.title: Add a reference still when accuracy matters
steps.desc: Upload a clean product, poster, character, or layout image when the logo, shape, silhouette, or composition should stay recognizable.

steps.title: Keep the useful result
steps.desc: Save variants with a clear signal. If the motion is crowded or the product becomes hard to read, rewrite the brief before spending more credits.

faq.q: Why is Wan 2.5 the cheaper Wan starting point?
faq.a: Wan 2.5 starts at 120 Credits for 720p 5-second output. Use it when the first decision is whether an idea deserves more spend.

faq.q: How many hook variants should I test before spending more?
faq.a: Run two to four small variants with different openings, product angles, or sound cues. Keep only the one with the clearest first-second signal.

faq.q: Can Wan 2.5 animate a product or poster still?
faq.a: Yes. Upload one clear still when a package, logo, poster layout, character silhouette, or thumbnail composition should stay recognizable during a small movement test.

faq.q: Should I choose 5 seconds or 10 seconds?
faq.a: Choose 5 seconds for the cheapest hook check. Choose 10 seconds only when the motion needs a second beat, such as slide then stop, pour then settle, or sparkle then hold.

faq.q: What should I do with weak Wan 2.5 results?
faq.a: Treat weak results as useful rejection data. If the logo breaks, the motion feels crowded, or the hook is unclear, discard the direction instead of polishing it.
Yes, but keep sound cues simple: fizz, tap, crinkle, pour, scrape, click, fabric rustle, or a short room tone.
Use one subject, one small motion, one camera behavior, and one sound or texture cue. The prompt should answer a narrow creative question instead of describing a full story.

faq.q: When should I stop using Wan 2.5 for an idea?
faq.a: Stop when the result cannot keep the logo readable, the motion feels crowded, or the creative question needs a complete sequence instead of a micro test.

modelComparison.title: Wan 2.5 Lower-Cost Testing Checklist
modelComparison.subtitle: Use this table to decide whether a small test should run, be rewritten, or stop before more credits are spent.

rows.label: Budget role
rows.baseline: Cheap first pass for hooks, product motion, poster animation, thumbnails, and sound texture.
rows.target: Full campaign story, multi-scene plan, or exact final composition is not ready for this option.

rows.label: Credit control
rows.baseline: 120 Credits at 720p / 5s keeps early testing contained.
rows.target: Delay extra spend until one hook or product motion is clearly worth it.

rows.label: Input shape
rows.baseline: Short text prompt or one clean still with a single subject.
rows.target: Too many references, crowded layouts, or long storyboard notes.

rows.label: Output length
rows.baseline: 5 or 10 second clips for quick judgment.
rows.target: Needs full narrative pacing instead of a simple signal check.

rows.label: Good signal
rows.baseline: Readable logo, clear motion, useful sound cue, and a clean hold.
rows.target: Broken branding, crowded movement, or unclear first-second hook.

rows.label: Next action
rows.baseline: Keep the winner and save the exact prompt notes.
rows.target: Rewrite the prompt, change the still, or stop spending on that direction.

promptExamples.title: Wan 2.5 Lower-Cost Test Prompts
promptExamples.subtitle: Copy these when you want to test an idea before spending more production credits.

items.title: Product Turn Test
items.prompt: Use the uploaded product photo for a five-second paid-social test. Rotate the bottle a few degrees, flash the label once, add a soft tabletop tap, and stop on a readable logo. Plain background, tiny movement, no extra story.
items.description: Checks whether a simple product motion is worth a stronger render.

items.title: Poster Motion Test
items.prompt: Turn the uploaded campaign poster into a short test clip. Add subtle paper lift, one narrow light sweep across the headline, and tiny metallic sparkle near the offer. Keep all text placement stable and use just enough movement to decide whether the still earns another pass.
items.description: Checks whether a static visual has useful animation potential.

items.title: Sound Texture Check
items.prompt: Create a tight close-up of sparkling water poured into a glass on a clean counter. Keep the setup simple for testing only. Add fizz, ice clink, liquid pour, and a small glass tap so the texture cue can be accepted or rejected fast.
items.description: Uses Wan 2.5 to test a simple sound-and-texture idea.

items.title: Keep-or-Rewrite Hook
items.prompt: Make a short test of a phone case sliding into view, catching one highlight, then stopping in the center. Use a plain backdrop, no extra story beats, and a clear ending hold. The goal is to decide whether this simple hook deserves another paid render.
items.description: Turns an early hook into a clear keep-or-rewrite decision.

troubleshooting.title: Prompt Tips for Wan 2.5 Tests
troubleshooting.subtitle: Keep Wan 2.5 prompts narrow so each run answers one creative question.

items.title: Ask one yes/no question
items.desc: Weak prompt: make a cool commercial. Better prompt:
items.prompt: Test only the opening hook: a compact serum bottle enters from the left, catches one clean highlight, and stops with the label readable. Plain backdrop, no scene change, one soft glass tap at the end.

items.title: Avoid full storyboards
items.desc: Weak prompt: show the whole launch journey. Better prompt:
items.prompt: Create a short shelf-test clip for one snack bag. The bag lifts slightly, the corner crinkles, and a small shadow moves under it. Keep the camera locked and use a quick paper-crinkle cue.

items.title: Use rejection language
items.desc: Weak prompt: make this perfect. Better prompt:
items.prompt: Generate a rough budget test only. If the logo becomes unreadable or the movement feels crowded, reject the concept instead of polishing it. Keep the action small and easy to judge.
